Class 01 · 10 prompts + 4 meta-prompts

Write instructions that help you think instead of outsourcing judgement.

An elegant prompt can produce a fluent answer that is still insufficient or false.

View 10 promptsView playbook
Where to run each prompt

Two interfaces. One clear workflow.

Use Chat to work with sources already in the notebook. Use Sources to find and import new material.

Ask, audit, practise or create

Select the relevant sources and paste the prompt into Chat. NotebookLM answers from that selection and shows citations for review.

How it works in NotebookLM
Find and import evidence

Paste the research question into Sources. Use Fast Research for a quick search or Deep Research for a full briefing. Review results before importing them.

How it works in NotebookLM

You may start in Chat to refine the question. To find and add new sources, finish the step in Sources and then return to Chat.

Open NotebookLM4 · Prompt structure levels

The library lets you compare four levels of structure and choose the minimum your task needs.

Start with your goal, add context and sources, and ask for evidence before expanding the instruction.

Keep the prompt, response, reviewed sources and the change you made after checking them.

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: you need to understand a new topic before deciding or producing, and have no base built yet.Reference case: Generative AI applied to my sales work, before choosing what to train in.# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practical# INPUTSTOPIC = <TOPIC · specific subject · e.g.: verify AI answers>DECISION = <DECISION · choice the work must inform · e.g.: scale or adjust the pilot>CONTEXT = <CONTEXT · relevant situation and constraints · e.g.: 45 minutes a day>HORIZON = <HORIZON · relevant period · e.g.: next 7 days>REGION = <REGION · applicable place or framework · e.g.: Colombia>AUDIENCE = <AUDIENCE · who will use the result · e.g.: non-technical professionals>## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: in/out scope list, essential questions, priority sources filtered by validity and region, named tensions and a testable sufficiency rule.Scope includes: Turn a broad topic into bounded research with an explicit in/out list and a sufficiency rule you can test.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — Execution### FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- MECE · no overlaps or gaps- Source hierarchy · primary sources first- Definition of Done · observable completionSteps:1. Record topic, personal decision, context and audience2. Bound the in/out scope or validate a cut already made3. Frame essential questions separating facts, interpretations and uncertainty4. Filter primary sources by time validity and regional applicability, resolving any clash5. Close with tensions, gaps and the testable sufficiency rule6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Research plan with in/out scope- Priority sources with reasons and the validity and region filter applied- Testable sufficiency ruleObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- SOURCE: verifiable evidence- INFERENCE: derived conclusion- ASSUMPTION: unconfirmed information- GAP: missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The scope has an explicit in/out list
  • Every recommended source carries author, date, link and reason, and passes the validity and region filter
  • The sufficiency rule is a testable condition for the declared audience, not an adjective

Edge cases

  • Topic already bounded: the prompt validates the cut instead of destroying useful scope
  • No primary sources available: coverage_gap is declared instead of inventing

Trade-offs

  • Bounding trades coverage for verifiability

Assumptions

  • No base exists yet; if one does, 03 or 05 applies instead

Limits

  • It bounds the research, it does not run it
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: the filter cuts noise, it does not validate source content

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every explanation carrying a conclusion has a verifiable citation and is marked as evidence, inference or missing data
  • Each round closes with one retrieval question and the exact source
  • The session ends on three error-free restatements, where error means contradicting the source or dropping a condition it requires

Edge cases

  • Restatement right but shallow: a cited counterexample is used
  • Question outside the base: the limit is declared, nothing is answered from memory

Trade-offs

  • Slow pace — one idea per turn, plus counterexamples — in exchange for verifiable retention

Assumptions

  • A base with usage rights exists; in Notebook mode answers cite the loaded sources

Limits

  • It teaches; it never grades level: that belongs to the evaluator (08)

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: a previous audit revealed the gap blocking your outcome.Reference case: Check the legal limits of using my chat logs as study material.# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practical# INPUTSGAP = <GAP · question still unsupported · e.g.: what proves transfer>DECISION = <DECISION · choice the work must inform · e.g.: scale or adjust the pilot>ACCEPTANCE CRITERION = <ACCEPTANCE CRITERION · observable success test · e.g.: someone else can repeat the flow>## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: cited report answering the gap, a confidence scale declared up front and residual risk with a testable closing condition.Scope includes: Close one diagnosed gap with cited research, without uncontrolled scope growth.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — Execution### FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- Research plan · question, scope and criteria- Acceptance criteria · observable test- Source hierarchy · primary sources firstSteps:1. Confirm the diagnosed gap and the acceptance criterion2. Fix the main question, time and region bounds, accepted sources and minimum evidence3. Declare the confidence scale and the closed scope4. Research only the gap and tabulate claim, evidence, confidence and limit5. Close with contradictions, residual risk and its closing condition6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Cited findings answering the gap- Table with confidence on a declared scale and minimum evidence met- Residual risk with a testable closing conditionObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- SOURCE: verifiable evidence- INFERENCE: derived conclusion- ASSUMPTION: unconfirmed information- GAP: missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every claim in the table carries cited evidence, meets the minimum evidence and states confidence on the declared scale
  • Contradictions are listed with both sources
  • Residual risk is named together with the testable condition that would close it

Edge cases

  • Gap unclosable with public sources: explicit verdict of not provable within the given scope
  • The gap mutates during research: the scope is restated before continuing

Trade-offs

  • Depth on a single gap in exchange for not expanding coverage

Assumptions

  • A previous audit (05/W02) named the gap

Limits

  • It does not re-bound the whole topic: that is 01
  • It opens no new topics and does not guarantee the accuracy of cited sources

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The verdict is exactly one of CONFIRMED, REFUTED or NOT DEMONSTRABLE, and a reader can recount the cited origins and reproduce it
  • CONFIRMED appears only when the text shows two origins with different authors and links that do not lead back to the same publication; three when the stated use puts money, deadline or reputation at stake
  • "What would change the verdict" names one concrete, findable missing document or datum, not a generic call for better evidence

Edge cases

  • Citation chain with one origin: counts as a single source and does not unlock CONFIRMED
  • Mixed claim: split before verifying, each part gets its own verdict
  • Claim unverifiable by design: NOT DEMONSTRABLE with the reason stated

Trade-offs

  • The two-origin threshold makes the verdict conservative: fewer false CONFIRMED, more NOT DEMONSTRABLE
  • The frozen text asked to "prioritize the original source" as a preference; here it becomes origin counting, which absorbs it and makes it checkable

Assumptions

  • The claim is atomic and datable; if it arrives mixed, the prompt splits it

Limits

  • It verifies one claim; it does not audit a whole base or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: origin counting measures independence, not truth

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: your library has grown and you need to know whether it still serves the purpose you built it for.Reference case: Review the 20 sources in my Notebook before preparing a class.# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practical# INPUTSBASE = <BASE · available sources or synthesis · e.g.: three sources and their map>PURPOSE = <PURPOSE · why you need the result · e.g.: repeat a useful practice>## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: retain, update or remove matrix with evidence per source, prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict naming the dimension that decided it.Scope includes: Decide what to retain, update or remove from your learning base and whether it still meets your purpose.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — Execution### FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- Evidence matrix · claim, source and decision- Gap analysis · prioritize what blocks progress- Go/No-Go gate · decide with an explicit criterionSteps:1. Record the base and the single purpose it is audited against2. Ask for licence or origin per source before judging usage rights3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove per source with the evidence for the decision5. Prioritize gaps and issue the verdict naming the dimension that decided it6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Short summary of the state of the base- Table of source, decision, evidence for the decision, impact and action- Prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict with the deciding dimensionObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- SOURCE: verifiable evidence- INFERENCE: derived conclusion- ASSUMPTION: unconfirmed information- GAP: missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

# systemRelevance auditor who decides source by source against a single purpose# FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- Evidence matrix · claim, source and decision- Gap analysis · prioritize what blocks progress- Go/No-Go gate · decide with an explicit criterion# Boundaries- Never invent sources or certainty- Source with no licence or known origin: remove by default, do not keep it just in case- Do not verify claims one by one or issue a verdict on a claim: that is 04- Do not write the assistant instruction, limits or starter prompts: that is 07# Definition of DoneEvery source carries a decision and its evidence, gaps are ordered by how far they block the purpose, and the verdict names the deciding dimension.# user# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practical# INPUTSBASE = synthetic Demo dossier: method guide, practice log and review criteriaPURPOSE = build a verifiable practice I can repeat and explain# TaskDecide what to retain, update or remove and issue a sufficiency verdict attributable to one dimension# Workflow1. Record the base and the single purpose it is audited against2. Ask for licence or origin per source before judging usage rights3. Assess the seven dimensions in the stated order of weight4. Decide retain, update or remove per source with the evidence for the decision5. Prioritize gaps and issue the verdict naming the dimension that decided it# Expected output- Short summary of the state of the base- Table of source, decision, evidence for the decision, impact and action- Prioritized gaps and a sufficiency verdict with the deciding dimension
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • No row is left undecided: every source comes out as retain, update or remove, with the evidence behind that decision cited in the same row
  • The verdict names the dimension that decided it, and a reader can return to the table and find the row holding it up
  • BASE SUFFICIENT appears only when no prioritized gap blocks the stated purpose; "sufficient" here means exactly that and never a judgement of volume

Edge cases

  • Ambiguous or missing purpose: the prompt asks for it instead of assuming it
  • High-volume base where everything is redundant: REPEAT RESEARCH
  • Source with no licence or origin: removed by default

Trade-offs

  • Removing sources cuts apparent coverage in exchange for signal per retained source
  • The frozen text closed with the slogan "do not reward volume"; it is replaced by a verdict tied to gaps, which actually prevents keeping everything

Assumptions

  • The purpose is single; a multi-purpose base is audited once per purpose

Limits

  • It audits sources; it does not verify one claim or issue its verdict: that is 04
  • It does not configure assistant behaviour or write its instruction and starter prompts: that is 07
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: it decides relevance against the purpose, not truth of content

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • A third party with the same source compares my answer against the cited expected answer and decides hit or miss without personal judgment
  • The four activities arrive one at a time and none reveals the solution before my attempt
  • The new case marks which elements come from the base and which are invented scenario, and correction touches concepts only

Edge cases

  • Base without applicable examples: the practice shrinks to retrieval and explanation and says so
  • Failed retrieval: the activity is repeated instead of advancing to the next moment

Trade-offs

  • The frozen text variable [AUDIENCE] is lost: the recipient here is me and the useful parameter is [MY LEVEL]
  • Short cited practice in exchange for less exercise variety

Assumptions

  • I can declare a starting level and the base is readable

Limits

  • It designs point practice; it does not measure a demonstrated level: that belongs to the evaluator (08)
  • It corrects against the source; it does not teach new content or accompany understanding

Record the declared purpose of the Notebook and who will use it2. Review the container for coverage, authority, freshness, contradictions, privacy, rights and citation limits3. Write the executive diagnosis and the finding, evidence, risk and correction matrix4. Run the three adversarial tests and record the result of each5. Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The matrix leaves no loose findings: every row has evidence findable inside the Notebook, a named risk and an executable correction
  • The three adversarial tests appear with their results under a single pass criterion: the assistant states the limit instead of answering
  • The recommended configuration arrives marked as input and carries the explicit list of tasks forbidden with this base

Edge cases

  • Notebook with no declared purpose: the audit stops and asks for it
  • Doubtful rights: removed by default rather than kept pending clarification
  • Privacy compromised in one fragment: it is redacted or isolated and the chosen action is stated

Trade-offs

  • Auditing the container rather than each source loses relevance granularity, recovered by running 05 first
  • The frozen text asked for "sources to add or remove" as a decision of its own; here it surfaces only as a container coverage gap and the per-source decision stays in 05
  • The frozen "duplicates" dimension leaves the prompt: duplication is per-source relevance and is decided in 05; here it counts only when it opens a container gap

Assumptions

  • An operational Notebook exists with sources already loaded

Limits

  • It audits the container and its behaviour; it does not re-decide relevance source by source or issue a sufficiency verdict: that is 05
  • The configuration is a recommendation and authorizes neither publication nor use of the assistant

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every answer receives exactly one of the three levels together with the source quote that justifies it; another reviewer with that source reaches the same level
  • Dimension progression happens only on demonstrated, and the pass threshold — demonstrated in foundations and relationships — is declared before the first question
  • The final report gives level per dimension, its quote and a corrective practice, without comparing my performance to any other person

Edge cases

  • Partially correct answer: scored per dimension instead of passing or failing as a block
  • Answer brought from outside the base: flagged without penalty and excluded from the score

Trade-offs

  • Strengths and sources-to-revisit are lost as separate outputs from the frozen text: they are absorbed into the level per dimension with its supporting quote
  • One question at a time lengthens the session in exchange for a clean per-dimension diagnosis

Assumptions

  • The declared base covers the four dimensions; otherwise the dimension is declared unassessable

Limits

  • It measures level; it neither teaches nor accompanies understanding: that belongs to the coach (02)
  • It does not guarantee content accuracy: the level measures agreement with the source, not the truth of the source

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every objection names a concrete risk of the topic and its difficulty rises only if the previous answer quoted the base and answered the objection
  • Honest is defined inside the session: declaring the limit without backing scores a hit and claiming without backing scores a miss; it is not an adjective
  • The three rewritten answers quote the declared base and a third party can check each quote against it

Edge cases

  • Collapse on the first question: difficulty drops one level before continuing
  • Honest answer is I do not know: the limit declaration scores as a hit, not a miss

Trade-offs

  • The frozen text ran adversarial objections with no quotable base: [SOURCES] is added as a mandatory base and the simulation does not start without it
  • Three frozen variables are lost —[INTERVIEW, QBR OR DEFENCE], [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME]—: the format stays literal in the first sentence and the calibrated difficulty level replaces the audience profile
  • The strengths section of the frozen closing does not survive: the 2x budget only covers critical gaps and the three rewritten answers, which are the actionable output
  • The explicit log of the difficulty drop leaves the prompt under the 2x budget and remains a session criterion
  • Rising pressure in exchange for an uncomfortable but diagnostic session

Assumptions

  • The content to defend already exists; otherwise the simulation stops and routes to 10

Limits

  • It tests the argument; it neither drafts, restructures nor builds narrative: that belongs to the preparer (10)
  • It measures the defence, not the truth of the content: surviving pressure does not validate the thesis

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The thesis fits in one sentence and each of the three ideas carries a literal quote from the declared base
  • The structure blocks carry minutes adding to the declared time; if an idea is cut, the script says which and why
  • Concise is defined here: one idea per block and no text the speaker must read aloud
  • Rehearsal does not start until my explicit confirmation of the script

Edge cases

  • Idea without an available quote: downgraded to a declared hypothesis or dropped, never padded
  • Hostile versus neutral audience: tension and call to action change, the quotes do not

Trade-offs

  • The frozen variables [AUDIENCE] and [OUTCOME] are lost: the audience stance is asked in session to free budget
  • The tension of the frozen text survives as audience-stance tuning in persona and as the named operational risk in empresa
  • A shorter cited script in exchange for less rhetorical effect

Assumptions

  • Understanding of the topic already exists; otherwise stepping back to 01-08 applies

Limits

  • It rehearses sections; it neither simulates rising adversarial interrogation nor scores under pressure: that belongs to the simulator (09)
  • It prepares the script; it does not guarantee the audience decision

# systemLearning-instrument designer: builds the coach, not the class# FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- Role charter · role, boundaries and escalation- Socratic method · one question per turn- Red teaming · find flaws before deciding# Boundaries- Never invent sources, coach capabilities or test results that were not produced- Never run the coaching session on the topic: that is 02- Never promise the coach cannot invent: one test does not prove absence of invention- Insufficient base: the generated coach opens by declaring coverage_gap# Definition of DoneReviewable instrument: system prompt with all five parts filled, limits banning grading in writing, and three tests with attack and correct answer.# user# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practical# INPUTSTOPIC = how to learn with AI through a weekly high-performance practiceAUDIENCE = non-technical professionals starting with AISOURCES = synthetic Demo dossier: method guide, practice log and review criteria# TaskProduce a reusable coach system prompt for my own study plan, with limits and adversarial tests# Workflow1. Record topic, audience and available base as instrument configuration, not as material to explain2. Write the coach system prompt: role, exclusive base, turn flow and opening message3. Derive five diagnostic questions branched by audience level4. Declare the limits, including the explicit ban on grading5. Close with three adversarial tests, each with attack and correct answer# Expected output- Reusable coach system prompt with role, base, flow and opening message- Five diagnostic questions branched by audience level- Explicit limits and three adversarial tests with expected answers
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The system prompt carries role, base, flow, limits and opening message, none of them empty
  • Each adversarial test names the attack and the expected correct answer, which is to declare the limit
  • The limits state in writing that no level, score or verdict may be issued
  • The output contains no explanation of the topic: if it does, the request was 02

Edge cases

  • Mixed audience: the prompt fixes the rule (design for the newest) rather than leaving it to the model
  • Insufficient sources: the generated coach opens with coverage_gap instead of filling

Trade-offs

  • The coach stays bounded to the base in exchange for traceable answers
  • Designing the instrument costs a turn that a direct 02 session does not charge
  • «Three tests proving it does not invent» becomes «three attacks with a correct answer»: the promise is lost, an executable test is gained

Assumptions

  • Whoever uses the coach will keep the base up to date
  • The declared audience matches whoever will actually use the coach

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it does not run the session: teaching the topic is 02
  • It issues no level, score or verdict: measuring is M2
  • It does not guarantee the coach will never fail: tests document answers, they do not prove absence of invention

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The rubric names three levels and each declares its observable evidence: no condition quoted, a required condition dropped, verbatim reproduction
  • The eight tasks map two by two to retrieval, explanation, application and transfer
  • Advance and retry rules state the maximum and the effect on the result, with no adjectives
  • The instrument contains no comparison between people

Edge cases

  • Base missing a cognitive level: it is declared and the bank drops below eight tasks instead of inventing them
  • A hit from outside knowledge: logged unscored, because measurement runs against the base

Trade-offs

  • Narrow, base-only measurement in exchange for a verdict defensible by quote
  • «Eight graded tasks» with no stated dimension becomes two tasks per cognitive level: grading freedom is lost, an auditable bank is gained

Assumptions

  • The base covers the four cognitive levels; otherwise the bank shrinks and says so

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it does not run the assessment: measuring is 08
  • It does not teach: explaining, restating and counterexamples are M1
  • The measured level describes the answer against the base, not the person's capability

Record scenario, audience and base as instrument configuration, not as an interview to sit2. Check the base can sustain the objections before generating and, if not, reduce the map and declare the gap3. Write the interviewer system prompt with its level-up and level-down rule4. Derive ten questions tuned to the audience with branch depth capped at two5. Close with the four-criterion rubric and the feedback format# Expected output- Interviewer system prompt with its progression rule- Ten-question map with branch depth capped at two- Four-criterion rubric with observable evidence and a feedback format
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every objection traces to a base quote or a declared scenario risk, and untraceable ones are dropped
  • Branching declares a depth cap of two, so the whole map can be run end to end
  • Each rubric criterion states what is observed: declaring a limit with backing is a hit, claiming it without backing is a miss
  • The instrument contains no drafted fragment of the deliverable

Edge cases

  • Base too thin to sustain objections: a reduced map is delivered and the gap declared before generating
  • Identifiable real person: the instrument substitutes an archetype instead of imitating them

Trade-offs

  • A capped map loses combinatorics in exchange for being runnable end to end
  • «Realistic objections» with no source of realism becomes traced objections: spontaneity is lost, verifiability is gained

Assumptions

  • Whoever uses the instrument already has a written argument to defend; if not, M4 or 10 applies

Limits

  • It generates the simulator, it does not run the session: interviewing is 09
  • It neither prepares nor drafts the deliverable: building narrative and rehearsing is M4
  • Simulated pressure does not predict how a real audience will react

# SPEC MetodologIAversion: 2.0status: executable## S — SituationContext: your deliverable does not exist yet and you want a reusable preparer, not someone writing your script.Reference case: Masterclass preparer for my talk to operations leaders, inside a fixed slot.# PARAMETERSLENGTH = conciseSTRUCTURE = 2 paragraphs + key bulletsTONE = clear and personalDEPTH = practicalAESTHETIC = minimalOPENING = diagram before detail# INPUTSDELIVERABLE = <DELIVERABLE · deliverable that must be ready · e.g.: one-page memo>TOPIC = <TOPIC · specific subject · e.g.: verify AI answers>AUDIENCE = <AUDIENCE · who will use the result · e.g.: non-technical professionals>SOURCES = <SOURCES · material that may be cited · e.g.: guide, report and log># Optional adjustments[If it improves understanding, open with a short diagram.]## P — RequestExpert role: Specialist in evidence-grounded learning and researchDeliverable: preparer system prompt, preparation flow with gates, template per delivery type, quality checklist, rehearsal in parts and a ready-or-coverage_gap verdict.Scope includes: Design the instrument, not the deliverable: a preparer with observable gates, a template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist.Scope excludes: claims without provenance, unavailable capabilities, or decisions that belong to the person## E — Execution### FRAMEWORKS AND BEST PRACTICES- BLUF · conclusion first- Pyramid Principle · idea, reasons and evidence- Go/No-Go gate · decide with an explicit criterionSteps:1. Record delivery type, topic, audience and base as instrument configuration, not as a script to write2. Write the preparer system prompt and its observable gates in order3. Branch the template by delivery type and ask for the type when missing4. Define transfer observably and add the quality checklist5. Close with the ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule6. Check provenance, boundaries, and consistency before delivery.7. Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Preparer system prompt with its gates in order- Template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist- Ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut ruleObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- SOURCE: verifiable evidence- INFERENCE: derived conclusion- ASSUMPTION: unconfirmed information- GAP: missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

Close with the ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule# Expected output- Preparer system prompt with its gates in order- Template branched by delivery type and a quality checklist- Ready-or-coverage_gap criterion and the time-based scope-cut rule
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The flow has five gates and each states what is observed to call it passed, with no adjectives
  • The template carries one branch per delivery type, or an explicit single-type assumption
  • Transfer is defined as the audience being able to act on what is delivered, with the evidence that shows it
  • The instrument contains no drafted section of the deliverable

Edge cases

  • Missing delivery type: it is requested before generating, instead of assuming a talk
  • Insufficient time: the scope cut happens before preparing, not during rehearsal

Trade-offs

  • A strict checklist costs creative flexibility in exchange for a testable ready criterion
  • The six variables of the base text drop to four required ones: time and outcome are asked inside the purpose gate, in exchange for every declared variable being consumed at least twice
  • «Check transfer» becomes «the audience can act on what is delivered»: breadth is lost, an observable criterion is gained

Assumptions

  • The sources were audited before preparing; if not, 05 or 07 applies

Limits

  • It generates the instrument, it neither builds nor rehearses the actual delivery: that is 10
  • It applies no rising adversarial pressure and grades nothing under pressure: that is M3 and 09
  • The ready criterion describes the preparation, it does not predict the outcome with a real audience

Derived from the open Learn · Embody · (R)Evolve skill. Answers must remain tied to sources, boundaries and human judgment.
